question.text: The US also occupied this country after the Spanish-American War, though they did not annex it. The CIA tried to use an exploding cigar and a tuberculosis-infected scuba suit to kill Fidel Castro, a Communist who led this country during the Cold War.
question.clue: Ramon Grau replaced Gerardo Machado in this nation in 1933 after the Coup of September, better known as the Sargeant's Revolt.

swap.leadin: This man's political supporters were derogatorily nicknamed the descamisados, or "shirtless ones."
swap.text: Name this populist president of a South American country who regained power in 1973 after being overthrown in 1955. This man legalized women's suffrage while being influenced by his wife, Evita.
swap.clue: This politician's left-wing supporters were killed at an airport in the Ezeiza (ayz-ay-EE-zah) massacre.

question.leadin: This general's army was once held up by a barking dog, which was then given to this general as a pet.
question.text: Name this general, known as "El Libertador" for his role in securing the independence of many South American countries, such as his native Venezuela.
question.clue: This man, who wrote the Letter from Jamaica while in exile, issued the Decree of War to the Death during the Admirable campaign.

swap.text: This next largest Caribbean island, the most populous island in the Americas, contains the nations of Haiti and the Dominican Republic.
swap.clue: After independence, this location was home to a separatist movement called La Trinitaria, which was led by Juan Pablo Duarte.

question.text: On this island, the colono sugar farmer class emerged with the opening of its first sugar mill in 1873. Ponce de Leon was the first governor of this island, which was defended by a fort called El Morro.
question.clue: Revolutionaries from this place uttered the "Grito de Lares" and used the Blair House to stage an unsuccessful assassination attempt on Harry Truman.

swap.text: Not long after Columbus' voyages, this friar sailed over to the New World, where he wrote A Short Account of the Destruction of the Indies after being appalled by the brutal encomienda system.
swap.clue: Protestant apologists drew on this man's work to create the "Black Legend."

question.text: This island was the site of Tacky's revolt in 1760. In 1831, this island was also the site of a slave rebellion led by Samuel Sharpe, the Baptist War, also known as the Christmas uprising.
question.clue: Simon Bolivar advocated for a united Latin America in a letter from this island, where he was exiled to in 1815.

swap.text: Haiti's independence movement from France was led by this man who was later betrayed by Jean-Jacques Dessalines.
swap.clue: This man is quoted as saying "In overthrowing me, you have cut down only the tree trunk of liberty" upon his arrest in 1802 by Jean-Baptiste Brunet.

question.text: Following World War II, Ante Pavelic fled to this country, where he was killed by a Montenegrin in 1957. Adolf Eichmann (IKE-mahn) was captured in this Latin American country, which has a sun on its flag.
question.clue: Juan Carlos Ongania established a military government in this country, whose transitional replacement, Hector Campora, fell from power after snipers fired on gathered crowds at an airport in the Ezeiza Massacre.

swap.text: In 1888, the Law of the Free Womb was expanded by this terse declaration of Pedro that immediately ended Brazilian slavery.
swap.clue: This 1888 law signed by Princess Isabel while her father Pedro II was outside of Brazil. It abolished slavery and agitated wealthy landlords in Minas Gerais ("meen-ah zher-ays"), who later backed an 1889 Republican coup.

question.leadin: There have been many Mexican revolutionaries and freedom fighters throughout history.
question.text: Name this leader of the Morelos-based Liberation Army of the South whose Plan of Ayala denounced Francisco Madero. A modern-day Chiapas-based militant group has a name inspired by the demonym given to followers of this man.
question.clue: This man formed the agrarian armed force the Liberation Army of the South.

swap.leadin: Identify the following about a rebel group.
swap.text: This Sandinista leader, who continues to be active in Nicaraguan politics, was president from 1984 until 1990 when he was defeated by Violeta Barrios de Chamorro.
swap.clue: In 1990, Pedro Chamorro's widow Violetta defeated this Sandanista ruler in the first free presidential elections in over fifty years.

question.leadin: These settlements were heralded by Voltaire as "the triumph of humanity" after Antonio Ruiz de Montoya popularized them in Europe in The Spiritual Conquest of Paraguay.
question.text: Give this name for South American Jesuit missions that protected over one hundred thousand native Guarani from Portuguese bandeirantes, but forced them to give up most tribal traditions.
question.clue: What places primarily in modern-day Paraguay were home to many Tupi and Chiquito people in the 17th and 18th centuries? They resisted slave raiders and enjoyed economic success before dying out in the 1760s.

swap.leadin: In order to stave off capture, this man hid in a Vatican embassy while American troops blasted rock music at the building.
swap.text: Identify this Latin American dictator and former CIA informant who in 2007 was extradited to France after being overthrown by the US in Operation Just Cause back in 1989.
swap.clue: He was simultaneously a paid informant for the CIA and the chief of military intelligence appointed by Omar Torrijos, and spied for Castro's Cuba.

question.leadin: This politician was a dictator for fifteen years; he subsequently made a comeback and served three years as a democratically elected president.
question.text: Name this nationalist and populist who presided over the Estado Novo in Brazil.
question.clue: This Brazilian ordered the dissolution of Congress and ushered in a period of authoritarianism known as the Estado Novo, which lasted during his time as dictator and president from 1930 to 1954.

swap.leadin: The Revolt of the Lash started on this battleship that was the first of its class and sparked an early 20th century South American naval arms race.
swap.text: Name this battleship whose sister ship, the Sao Paulo, shelled a mutinous Fort Copacabana. The "milk interests" of its namesake state's dairy industry complemented Sao Paulo's "coffee" interests in the "coffee with milk" system.

question.text: Many Latin American Jesuits identified "men for others" with the preferential option for the poor, a doctrine espoused by this founder of liberation theology in On the Side of the Poor and We Drink from the Wells.
question.clue: James Cone's work on black liberation theology predates this Peruvian priest's book A Theology of Liberation, which articulated the "preferential option for the poor" and launched the liberation theology movement in Latin America.

swap.leadin: Rodrigo Carazo repealed a law in this country that was passed specifically to prevent the extradition of the fugitive American fraudster Robert Vesco.
swap.text: Name this country where the legislature's annulment of Otilio Ulate's election victory sparked a 1948 civil war. This country abolished its military after that war, which toppled the government of Teodoro Picado.
swap.clue: After failing to claim conscientious objector status from the U.S. government, Quakers from Alabama moved to the town of Monteverde in this country.

question.text: In the leadup to Boyaca, Simon Bolivar pulled out a crucial victory at this swamp over Jose Maria Barreiro.

swap.text: A civil war was fought in El Salvador in the 1980s that ended with the 1992 Peace of Chapultepec, which recognized this leftist organization, formed by the merger of the FPL, PCS, PRS, and RN organizations. This league is named for a Communist who was killed during the Matanza.
swap.answerHtml: FMLN [or Frente Farabundo Marti para la Liberacion Nacional; or Farabundo Marti National Liberation Front]
swap.clue: This former rebel group that fought ORDEN death squads during its country's civil war. Since the Chapultepec Peace Accords, it has competed against the ARENA party for a majority in the legislature.
